rounds.text: JSW Steel Ltd trades at a P/E of 9.56x against a sector benchmark of 15.44x, alongside an EV/EBITDA of 6.66x compared to its sector benchmark of 9.32x [E6, E11]. A discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 1,772 per share against the market price of Rs 1,255, offering a margin of safety of 29.2% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price implies a negative earnings growth of -1.9%, which sits below the base case assumption of 3.0% growth [E47]. Operational execution remains robust, evidenced by a dramatic surge in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months to 157% [E21] and a TTM operating margin expanding to 17% [E30]. Balance sheet strength has markedly improved as borrowings dropped significantly from Rs 99,310 Cr to Rs 69,820 Cr over a single year [E39], supported by strong free cash flow generation of Rs 10,610 Cr [E36]. Conceded: the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 2.71x, which exceeds the sector benchmark of 1.86x [E2, E7], and promoters have slightly trimmed their holdings by 0.52 percentage points since Dec 2023 [E41].

The business exhibits clear structural growth deceleration, highlighted by a compounded sales growth of just 4% over 3 years [E16] and a meager 3% compounded profit growth over 5 years [E19]. Compounded median return on equity has compressed to 9% over the last 3 years [E28], alongside a low 3-year return on equity of 8.97% [E62]. Furthermore, operating-margin trends are explicitly flagged as inconsistent across both yearly (3-year) and quarterly (2-quarter) horizons [E32, E33], reflecting acute cyclical vulnerability. Valuation risks are compounded by a price-to-book ratio of 2.71x [E2] which exceeds the sector benchmark of 1.86x [E7], and reported earnings carry a heavy reliance on a massive Rs. 19,430 Cr of other income [E63]. Historical volatility is exceptionally severe, with annualised volatility at 46.9% [E54] and a devastating worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -87.7% [E53]. Conceded: the company has reduced debt [E59], holds a moderate leverage of 0.62x [E37], and demonstrated strong recent TTM profit growth of 157% [E21].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years is 4% [E16] and 5-year profit growth is 3% [E19]. However, those lagging figures ignore the massive structural acceleration currently underway, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 157% [E21] and a stellar rules-based screen score of 82 out of 100 [E64]. While the bear points to a compressed 3-year median return on equity of 9% [E28], the company's broader operational efficiency significantly outclasses the broader sector, delivering an ROCE of 14.58% against a sector benchmark of 10.45% [E10] and an ROA of 12.55% against 5.25% [E8]. Conceded: operating-margin trends are flagged as inconsistent [E32, E33], yet the actual operating margin has expanded to 17% in the TTM and reached 19% in the September 2026 quarter [E30, E31]. The concern over valuation multiples is neutralized by a bargain EV/EBITDA of 6.66x compared to the sector benchmark of 9.32x [E11] and a P/E of just 9.56x against a sector benchmark of 15.44x [E6]. Finally, historical drawdown risks [E53] are actively being mitigated as the company aggressively reduces its borrowings down to Rs 69,820 Cr from Rs 99,310 Cr a year earlier [E39, E59].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 157% [E21] and ROCE stands at 14.58% against a sector benchmark of 10.45% [E10]. However, that short-term burst obscures a dismal structural track record, featuring a 3-year compounded sales growth of just 4% [E16] and a stagnant 5-year profit growth of 3% [E19]. While the bull celebrates an operating margin of 17% in the TTM and 19% in Sep 2026 [E30, E31], filed statements explicitly warn that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends read inconsistent [E32, E33]. The bull's highlighted P/E and EV/EBITDA discounts ignore glaring valuation traps elsewhere, specifically a price-to-book ratio of 2.71x [E2] that trades at a substantial premium to the sector benchmark of 1.86x [E7]. Furthermore, the company's recent earnings are heavily contaminated by an unsettling other income component of Rs 19,430 Cr [E63]. Finally, pointing to debt reduction [E39, E59] fails to excuse a median return on equity of a depressed 9% over the last 3 years [E28] alongside a staggering historical peak-to-trough drawdown risk of -87.7% [E53].
